metadata.chief_complaint: well-child checkup and sick visit for cough and congestion

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: Good morning! I'm Dr. Martinez. Emma, it's nice to see you again. How are you feeling today?

script.speaker: child
script.text: My nose is stuffy and I have a cough.

script.speaker: mom
script.text: She's been coughing for about four days now, and the congestion started maybe two days ago. I wasn't sure if we should wait or bring her in.

script.speaker: dad
script.text: The cough seems worse at night. She was up a few times last night.

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: I understand your concern. Let's talk about the cough first, and then we'll do her regular four-year checkup. Has she had any fever?

script.speaker: mom
script.text: No fever that I've noticed. I've been checking pretty regularly.

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: That's good. Any runny nose or change in appetite?

script.speaker: dad
script.text: Her nose has been pretty runny, clear stuff mostly. She's been eating okay, maybe a little less than usual.

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: Emma, can you tell me if your throat hurts or if it's hard to swallow?

script.speaker: child
script.text: It doesn't hurt. Just coughy.

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: Okay, sweetie. Let me listen to your chest first. Can you take some big breaths for me?

script.speaker: child
script.text: Like this?

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: Perfect! You're doing great. Her lungs sound clear, which is reassuring. Let me check her ears and throat now.

script.speaker: mom
script.text: Do you think it's just a cold? I worry about her missing preschool.

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: Let me finish the exam and we'll talk about that. Emma, can you open your mouth wide like a lion? Say 'ahh'.

script.speaker: child
script.text: Ahhhhh!

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: Excellent! Her throat looks fine, just a little red. Ears look good too. This does appear to be a viral upper respiratory infection - a common cold.

script.speaker: dad
script.text: So antibiotics won't help then?

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: That's right. Since it's viral, antibiotics won't be effective. The good news is these typically resolve on their own in seven to ten days.

script.speaker: mom
script.text: What can we do to help her feel better? And when can she go back to school?

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: For comfort, you can use saline nose drops, a cool mist humidifier, and honey for the cough if needed - just a half teaspoon. She can return to school when she's fever-free for 24 hours.

script.speaker: dad
script.text: Since she hasn't had a fever, could she go back tomorrow?

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: If she's feeling well enough and the cough isn't too disruptive, yes. Now let's move on to her regular four-year checkup. How has her development been?

script.speaker: mom
script.text: She's doing really well. Potty trained, knows her colors and letters, plays well with other kids.

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: That's wonderful. Any concerns about her behavior, sleep, or eating habits?

script.speaker: dad
script.text: She's been sleeping through the night, except for this week with the cough. Eats pretty well, maybe a little picky sometimes.

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: Emma, let me check how tall you've grown. Can you stand up straight against this wall for me?

script.speaker: child
script.text: Am I bigger?

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: You are! You've grown two inches since last year. You're right on track. She'll need some vaccines today - her four-year immunizations.

script.speaker: mom
script.text: Which ones does she need?

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: She needs DTaP, IPV, MMR, and Varivax boosters. These help protect her before starting kindergarten.

script.speaker: dad
script.text: Will she be okay to get them with this cold?

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: Yes, mild cold symptoms don't prevent vaccination. Emma, you're going to get some quick shots to keep you healthy, okay?

script.speaker: child
script.text: Will it hurt?

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: Just for a second, like a quick pinch. You're such a brave girl, and your mom and dad will be right here with you.
